conviction_note: Small positive lean (p_up 57 on a 4.0% absolute move, scaled +0.56; findings sum +1.85). It rests on a peer reading: State Street printed after BNY's CFO last spoke on Sep 14, and its Q3 NII and revenue held roughly flat on Q2 while BNY's consensus models a 2-3% sequential decline. Against it, State Street fell 6.4% on a print that raised guidance, so the sector is currently being sold on its prints, and BNY's entry already carries a 3.6% sympathy drop that cuts both ways. The findings sum is about three times the scaled number because each finding carries its full size while p_up absorbs the doubt about the reaction; the two measurements are not fitted to each other.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $2.26 (Zacks, https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:f0cf352fc094b:0-growth-in-fee-income-higher-nii-likely-to-support-bny-s-q3-earnings/), $2.27 (Hudson Labs, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/bny-q3-2026-earnings-revenue-preview-guidance-key-metrics, and Benzinga), $2.25 (TickerLeague). Revenue $5.56B (Zacks) or $5.546B (Hudson Labs); the sources agree, so the bar is sourced. Zacks puts fees and other revenue at $4.16B, which implies NII of about $1.40B against Q2's $1,446M. Company guide for FY2026 (from Q2): revenue +10-11%, NII +12-13%, expenses +6-7%, about 400bp of operating leverage. print_vs_bar is measured on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest about 7.5M shares (roughly 1% of shares outstanding), 1.9 days to cover, settlement 2026-07-15 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/bny/short-interest/). That figure is stale: Nasdaq's short-interest API returned 503, so nothing newer was found. Not a crowded short. Skew is +2.1 vol points, mild downside paid, on a 43%-of-mid ATM spread; put/call open interest 0.46. Tape: -11.3% over 20 days and -17.4% from the 52-week high. On 2026-10-14 the stock fell 3.6% (141.03 to 135.94, Yahoo chart) in sympathy with State Street's -6.4%.

findings.finding: State Street reported Q3 2026 on 10-14, after BNY's CFO last spoke on Sep 14. NII was $864M against $860M in Q2, so flat to up rather than down. Total revenue was about $4.0B against $4.048B in Q2, roughly -1% q/q. It raised FY NII guidance to 15-16% from 14-15% and FY fee guidance to 13-14% from 12-13%, put Q4 average deposits at $275-280B against an earlier $270B view, and reported FX +17% YoY on record volumes and securities finance +9%. BNY's consensus models revenue -2.4% q/q ($5.56B vs $5.698B) and NII about -3% q/q (~$1.40B vs $1,446M). If BNY tracks State Street's sequential pattern, it beats on revenue by about 1-1.5% and on NII by about 3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BNY bought its last two revenue/EPS beats: Q2 2026 EPS $2.46 vs $2.16 gave +5.08% (baseline), and Q1 2026 revenue $5.41B vs $5.19B gave +2.18% (https://stocks.observer-reporter.com/observerreporter/article/stockstory-2026-4-16-bny-nysebk-delivers-impressive-q1-cy2026). But the Q3 2025 beat drew -2.03%, and the peer itself sold 6.4% today on near-in-line numbers with raised guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: BNY's own consensus was set after the CFO's Sep 14 'Q3 slower, deposits slower' remarks and still sits 2-3% below Q2 on both revenue and NII. If the market had read State Street's flat sequential NII and higher deposit view across to BNY, BNY would have held up today. Instead it fell 3.6% in sympathy, which prices State Street's revenue miss and weak servicing sales into BNY rather than its NII and deposit strength.
findings.independence: State Street's own Q2 release gives the q/q base, NII $860M and revenue $4,048M (https://s203.q4cdn.com/888565246/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/STT-2Q26-Earnings-Press-Release-vFinal.pdf). JPMorgan raised its FY NII outlook on 10-13 (https://www.tikr.com/blog/jpmorgan-chase-stock-raises-net-interest-income-outlook-q3-2026, snippet_only). This is a peer proxy, not BNY's own number.

findings.finding: BNY's own FY2026 guide is set below the Street. FY2025 NII was $4,944M, so +12-13% gives $5,537-5,587M; H1 2026 NII was $2,816M, which leaves an implied H2 of $1,361-1,385M a quarter, below Q2's $1,446M and below the ~$1.40B Q3 consensus. Revenue +10-11% on $20,080M leaves an H2 average of $5.49-5.59B. With State Street and JPMorgan both raising NII outlooks this week, an NII (and likely revenue) guide raise tomorrow is the probable path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised the revenue guide to +10-11% from about +6% and NII to +12-13% from +10%, and the stock rose 5.08% that day (baseline; guide history from Hudson Labs). Q1 2026 also raised the NII guide, and the stock rose 2.18%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Consensus already sits above the guide-implied H2 NII run-rate, so the Street expects some raise, and that is why the size is small. What is not priced is how large the raise is: BNY trades at -17% from its high, down 3.1% on the day the CFO said he does 'not like to constantly re-guide' (Sep 14, https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/bny-mellon-at-barclays-conference-growth-ai-and-crosssell-push-93CH-4899943). A market expecting a raise would not have taken the stock down 14% since then.
findings.independence: FY2025 base from the Q4 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1390777/000139077726000004/ex991_earningsreleasex4q25.htm). Peer NII guide raises are the State Street transcript, which is the same document as finding 1 (so the two share a source), and JPMorgan via tikr (snippet_only).

findings.finding: BNY fell 3.6% on 2026-10-14 (141.03 to 135.94) in sympathy with State Street's 6.4% drop (174.10 to 162.93). State Street's drop was tied to a ~1% revenue miss from late-September mark-to-market in other fees and $68M of servicing sales, both State Street-specific metrics. So BNY enters its print with a peer-driven discount already in the price. A clean print recovers part of it; the same punitive reaction function would push a soft one lower.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BNY rose after 5 of its last 7 prints. The peer's reaction today, -6.4% on a print with raised NII and fee guides, is the counter-evidence that the sector is selling prints this season.
findings.why_not_priced: This is about where the bar now sits, not a hidden fact. If the market believed BNY carried none of State Street's issues, BNY would not have taken more than half of State Street's drop the day before its own print. The size is netted for the opposite reading, that the same mood sells BNY too.
findings.independence: State Street's tape is the same Yahoo chart source (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/STT?range=1mo&interval=1d). The drivers of State Street's drop come from the investing.com transcript, the same document as finding 1.

findings.finding: BNY's Q3 revenue was above Q2 last year (Q3 2025 $5,081M vs Q2 2025 $5,028M, +1%). This year consensus models -2.4% q/q, following the CFO's Sep 14 remarks that 'Q3 was slower than Q2' and 'deposits were slower in Q3, that is for sure', while he also said capital-markets volumes 'kicked back into September' and he feels 'pretty good about where that guide is'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 3.1% on the Sep 14 conference day (162.66 to 157.66). Q3 2025, when revenue rose q/q and beat, drew -2.03% on the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The company told the market to expect a softer Q3, so this lands inside what was guided, and the size is near zero. What is left is that a -2.4% q/q consensus is a lower sequential bar than BNY's own Q3 history or State Street's -1% q/q.
findings.independence: Q2/Q3 2025 revenue from the Q4 2025 release and the Q2 2026 release (SEC links above). State Street's q/q comes from finding 1's document.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp on 2026-09-16; BNY lifted its prime rate to 7.00% from 6.75% effective Sep 17. That gives about two weeks of higher floating asset yields in Q3 and supports Q4 NII. The CFO calls a ±100bp move 'negligible' to NII, and JPMorgan flagged deposit migration pressure in a higher-rate setting.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated; this is macro transmission.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public and largely priced. It is filed small as macro-to-company transmission that BNY itself describes as negligible to NII.
findings.independence: State Street's NIM was up 16bp YoY and it raised its NII guide (finding 1's document). This is a proxy.

baseline_tension: The lean is positive. That agrees with the 20-day run-up (-11.3%, expectations reset lower) and runs mildly against the +2.1 skew, which is small on a wide 43% spread. The strongest counter-evidence is the peer reacting -6.4% to raised guidance today, and that is why p_up stays at 57 rather than 60+.
lessons_applied: Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the sympathy-discount finding argues both ways (relief vs. a punitive sector reaction function), so it moved from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 6 (inside what was guided): the seasonality/CFO-warning finding lands inside what the company told the market on Sep 14, so it moved from +0.3 to +0.15.

Lesson 1 / reaction function: BNY bought its last two beats (+5.08, +2.18), so the peer reading was left at +0.8; State Street's -6.4% on raised guides moved p_up from 58 to 57, giving a scaled number of +0.56 instead of +0.64.

'What has worked' (a peer's print landing after the company last spoke, leaving consensus stale) supports keeping finding 1 at full size; lesson 5 (proxy) was already reflected in the draft size and was not applied twice.
Lesson 7: short interest was looked up (about 1%, not crowded); the skew is mild, so no change of sign.
